identification.summary: Manatee Tempest (formerly DEV-0243) is a financially motivated, ransomware-associated group that Microsoft says overlaps with activity other vendors track as EvilCorp [S2][S3]. Microsoft cites the Dridex banking trojan as one of the earliest campaigns that made the group notorious [S2]. CrowdStrike, tracking the group as INDRIK SPIDER, says it has operated Dridex since June 2014 and expanded into targeted 'big game hunting' ransomware with BitPaymer in 2017 [S5]. Microsoft says the group buys access from DEV-0206 (Mustard Tempest), supplies custom Cobalt Strike loaders, deployed WastedLocker, then in-house PhoenixLocker and Macaw, and from about November 2021 the LockBit 2.0 RaaS payload [S1][S3]. In October 2024 the UK NCA, with the US and Australia, sanctioned Evil Corp members and described links to Russian intelligence services [S10][S11].
identification.firstObserved: CrowdStrike: Dridex operations since June 2014 [S5]. Microsoft gives no first-seen date for Manatee Tempest [S2].
identification.notes: Microsoft name: Manatee Tempest; 'DEV-0243 is now tracked as Manatee Tempest' per Microsoft's April 2023 naming update [S2]. Microsoft's Security Insider profile lists EvilCorp as an alias [S3]. Mandiant tracks a highly overlapping cluster as UNC2165 and the FakeUpdates access chain separately as UNC1543 [S7]. CrowdStrike uses INDRIK SPIDER [S5][S13]. The access broker DEV-0206 / Mustard Tempest (SocGholish/FakeUpdates) is a separate Microsoft cluster that hands off access; do not merge their facts [S1]. Per the imported actor record, Microsoft's naming map also lists INDRIK SPIDER under Mustard Tempest; this record keeps Manatee Tempest as the Russia-origin ransomware cluster.

attribution.sponsor: Russia-based financially motivated criminal group with documented ties to Russian intelligence services, not a state unit. US Treasury (2019) said leader Maksim Yakubets worked for the FSB as of 2017 [S6]. The UK NCA (2024) said the group cultivated ties with the FSB, SVR and GRU, aided by Yakubets' father-in-law Eduard Benderskiy, a former senior official of the FSB's Vympel unit [S10].
attribution.confidence: Microsoft describes overlap between Manatee Tempest and EvilCorp, without a stated confidence level [S2]. Mandiant assesses with high confidence that UNC2165 shifted to LockBit to hinder attribution and evade sanctions, and calls UNC2165 highly likely the latest incarnation of Evil Corp [S7][S8]. State-link claims are made by US Treasury (2019) and the UK NCA (2024), not by Microsoft [S6][S10].
attribution.basis: US Treasury OFAC designations and DOJ indictments of Yakubets and Igor Turashev in December 2019, as reported [S6]; UK/US/Australian sanctions and a US indictment of Aleksandr Ryzhenkov in October 2024, as reported [S10][S11][S13]; Microsoft telemetry on DEV-0206 to DEV-0243 handoffs [S1][S2]; CrowdStrike and Mandiant malware and intrusion analysis [S5][S7].

objectives: Primarily financial: Dridex credential theft and wire fraud against banks, then ransomware extortion of organizations [S5][S6]. Treasury said Dridex losses exceeded $100 million [S6]. Secondary state-aligned tasking is alleged: Treasury said Yakubets was tasked with projects for the Russian state, including acquiring confidential documents through cyber means [S6], and the NCA, as reported, said Russian intelligence services tasked the group with cyber attacks and espionage operations against NATO allies [S10][S13]. Since 2021 the group has used RaaS brands such as LockBit to hide its identity and evade sanctions [S1][S7].

sectors: Organizations running domain-joined VMware ESXi hypervisors [S4]
regions: Global: Dridex victims in over 40 countries [S6]
targeting.notes: Targeting is opportunistic, shaped by the access DEV-0206/FakeUpdates infections provide, then narrowed to high-value organizations [S1][S5][S7]. NCC Group reportedly said the group did not steal or threaten to publish victim data in WastedLocker operations [S12]. Details of the alleged NATO espionage targets were not disclosed [S10].

capabilities.summary: Custom malware development across a decade: the Dridex banking trojan with repeated module and anti-analysis updates [S5]; BitPaymer ransomware, with Dridex typically installed before BitPaymer deployment [S5]; WastedLocker, Hades, PhoenixLocker and Macaw ransomware [S1][S3][S7]; and custom Cobalt Strike loaders resembling Blister inner payloads [S1]. Initial access commonly comes from the SocGholish/FakeUpdates chain run by DEV-0206/UNC1543, including FakeUpdates delivered through existing Raspberry Robin infections in 2022 [S1][S2][S7]. Hands-on-keyboard lateral movement resembles nation-state and penetration-testing tradecraft [S5]. Since about November 2021 the group has used the LockBit RaaS payload to avoid attribution [S1][S7]. In 2024 Microsoft named Manatee Tempest among ransomware operators using the 'ESX Admins' technique (CVE-2024-37085) to gain full control of domain-joined ESXi hypervisors [S4]. Aleksandr Ryzhenkov is reported to be a LockBit affiliate [S11][S13].

campaigns.name: Dridex banking trojan operations
campaigns.summary: CrowdStrike says INDRIK SPIDER has operated Dridex since June 2014; Treasury says Dridex harvested banking credentials from institutions in over 40 countries, causing more than $100 million in losses.

campaigns.name: BitPaymer big game hunting (UK NHS)
campaigns.summary: BitPaymer ransomed UK NHS organizations with a 53 BTC demand; CrowdStrike attributes BitPaymer to INDRIK SPIDER and estimates about $1.5M in its first 15 months.

campaigns.name: US sanctions and indictments of Evil Corp leaders
campaigns.summary: OFAC designated Evil Corp and Maksim Yakubets, citing his FSB work; DOJ indicted Yakubets and Igor Turashev, and the State Department offered a $5M reward.

campaigns.name: WastedLocker attack on Garmin
campaigns.summary: Garmin services were disrupted by WastedLocker ransomware, which NCC Group attributed to Evil Corp; a $10M demand was reported.

campaigns.name: Post-OFAC-advisory rebranding
campaigns.summary: Mandiant reports that WastedLocker activity stopped after an October 2020 OFAC advisory, and several closely related ransomware variants, including HADES, appeared in quick succession.

campaigns.name: Shift to LockBit 2.0 RaaS payload
campaigns.summary: Microsoft says the group began deploying LockBit 2.0 around November 2021, likely to avoid attribution tied to its sanctioned status; Mandiant reports the same shift for UNC2165.

campaigns.name: Raspberry Robin to FakeUpdates to DEV-0243 handoff
campaigns.summary: Microsoft observed FakeUpdates delivered through Raspberry Robin infections, followed by activity resembling DEV-0243 pre-ransomware behavior.

campaigns.name: ESXi 'ESX Admins' technique (CVE-2024-37085)
campaigns.summary: Microsoft names Manatee Tempest among ransomware operators using the ESX Admins group technique against domain-joined ESXi hypervisors.

campaigns.name: UK/US/Australia sanctions and Ryzhenkov indictment (Operation Cronos phase)
campaigns.summary: The NCA sanctioned 16 Evil Corp members and exposed ties to the FSB, SVR and GRU; the US indicted Aleksandr Ryzhenkov over BitPaymer and linked him to LockBit.

diamond.adversary: Russia-based Evil Corp operators led by Maksim Yakubets, with Igor Turashev and Aleksandr Ryzhenkov named by US and UK authorities [S6][S10][S13]; Microsoft tracks the cluster as Manatee Tempest [S3].
diamond.capability: Dridex, BitPaymer, WastedLocker, Hades, PhoenixLocker, Macaw, custom Cobalt Strike loaders, LockBit RaaS payloads, and ESXi hypervisor encryption via CVE-2024-37085 [S1][S3][S4][S5][S7].
diamond.infrastructure: Access bought from DEV-0206 SocGholish/FakeUpdates infections, including those delivered through Raspberry Robin [S1][S2]; LockBit affiliate infrastructure since 2021 [S1][S11].
diamond.victim: Banks and financial institutions in over 40 countries; healthcare and large enterprises such as Garmin [S5][S6][S12].
diamond.socioPolitical: Profit-driven crime under sanctions pressure, using RaaS brands to evade attribution [S1][S7]; tolerated and reportedly tasked by Russian intelligence services, including alleged espionage against NATO members [S6][S10][S13].
diamond.technology: Windows enterprise networks reached through browser-update lures and USB-worm footholds, plus domain-joined VMware ESXi hypervisors [S1][S2][S4].

gaps: Primary government documents (Treasury OFAC 2019 and 2024 releases, DOJ indictments, NCA 'Evil Corp: Behind the Screens' report) were not opened; details rely on press coverage of them.
Coverage of the NCA report differs on whether SVR and GRU ties were established or only sought. The nature, dates and targets of the alleged NATO espionage operations are undisclosed.
Microsoft gives no confidence level for the Manatee Tempest/EvilCorp overlap. Vendor cluster boundaries among Manatee Tempest, UNC2165 and INDRIK SPIDER may not coincide exactly.
Microsoft's naming map reportedly lists INDRIK SPIDER under both Manatee Tempest and Mustard Tempest (per imported record); the mapping file was not re-verified this session.
No public reporting from 2025-2026 on Manatee Tempest activity was found; current operational status, and whether the group still deploys LockBit after Operation Cronos, is unknown.
Garmin attribution to Evil Corp came from NCC Group as reported; Arete IR called the evidence inconclusive, and payment was never confirmed by Garmin [S12].
Which ransomware Manatee Tempest deployed in the 2024 ESXi attacks is not specified by Microsoft [S4].
CrowdStrike's October 2024 blog and The Register/Infosecurity coverage could not be fetched; claims from them rely on search-result summaries.

Fact-check 2026-10-14: a TechRadar source (since removed) not found in search and removed with its sole-sourced claims (earnings since 2011, at least $300M, CNI/government targeting). Microsoft S1-S4, CrowdStrike S5 and Computing S12 URLs were not re-verified by search this pass.

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1 (environment): Key terrain is enterprise Windows endpoints exposed to browser-update lures and removable media, Active Directory, and domain-joined ESXi hypervisors hosting mission systems [S1][S2][S4]. STEP 2 (effects): A single SocGholish or Raspberry Robin foothold can be sold onward, so commodity infections on DoD or DIB networks are pre-ransomware warning, not noise [S1][S2]. ESXi encryption can take down many virtualized services at once [S4]. STEP 3 (threat model): access broker handoff, Cobalt Strike loader, credential theft and lateral movement, then mass encryption under a RaaS brand that hides the operator [S1][S5][S7]. STEP 4: MLCOA is financially motivated ransomware against large organizations including healthcare, deployed under another brand's payload [S1][S5]. MDCOA is state-tasked intrusion against NATO-member targets under criminal cover, using ransomware access for espionage or disruption [S6][S10][S13]. Candidate indicators: fake browser update ZIP/JS downloads executed by wscript, Raspberry Robin USB LNK infections, unexpected Cobalt Strike beacons after those infections, and creation of an 'ESX Admins' AD group [S1][S2][S4].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. (1) Situational awareness: track SocGholish/FakeUpdates and Raspberry Robin detections across DODIN segments as leading indicators, and include ESXi/AD hygiene status in mission-assurance dashboards [S1][S2][S4]. (2) Authorities: Evil Corp and named members are under US, UK and Australian sanctions, so any ransom-payment discussion by mission partners or contractors raises OFAC issues; coordinate with legal before engaging [S6][S11]. Criminal-cover operations with alleged intelligence tasking blur the line between law enforcement and military response [S10][S13]. (3) Mission assurance: plan for simultaneous loss of virtualized services and test restoration of hypervisor clusters [S4]. (4) Coordination: brand-based attribution is unreliable because the group uses LockBit and other RaaS payloads, so share indicators with FBI, CISA, DC3 and coalition partners (NCA) and avoid naming an actor from the ransom note alone [S1][S7][S11].
